items.title: Our 2027 Innovators Under 35 competition is now open
items.raw_text: Every year, the editors at MIT Technology Review select 35 of the world’s top young scientists, entrepreneurs, and inventors to honor as our newest class of Innovators Under 35. And starting today, our 2027 competition is officially open for nominations. We’re on the hunt for researchers and founders who are engineering solutions to some of the most formidable problems society faces, including human disease and climate change. We also recognize those who have made clever and useful inventions, important new scientific discoveries, or technological breakthroughs early in their careers. We want to hear about people, based anywhere in the world, who are responsible for a major finding or advance and can show real-world impact from their work. To qualify for the list, a nominee must be under the age of 35 as of October 1, 2027 (that is, born on or after October 2, 1992). Have someone in mind? Or think you’d be a great candidate and want to nominate yourself? Follow this link to suggest someone who you think should make our 2027 list. It’s free and takes only a few minutes. Just be sure to get your nomination in before the deadline—which is 11:59 p.m. Eastern time on Tuesday, January 19. After the deadline, our editors will review all nominees and select a group of semifinalists, whom we’ll invite to complete a formal application. Then, dozens of expert judges will help us evaluate those applicants and settle on the finalists. You can read more about our selection process here . O

items.title: How cutting-edge prosthetics can help probe the human mind
items.raw_text: Over the last few weeks, I’ve been talking to Alexander (Avi) Davidson. There are a lot of remarkable things about Avi. He sustained a horrific injury as a teenager, which left him paralyzed and without a left hand. Today, he uses his own experience to guide his practice as a trauma therapist. He’s also taking part in a clinical trial of some new tech that allows him to move—and feel with—a prosthetic hand. Unlike standard prosthetics, this one connects directly to nerves in Avi’s arm . He literally has wires coming out of his arm to plug it in with. Avi’s the ninth person to trial this tech. But he’s the first to take it home and use it independently, for things like drinking from a cup (which is not easy ) and writing (also not easy ). What struck me the most over our conversations was Avi’s outlook and approach to not just his injuries and learning to use this cutting-edge technology, but to life itself. He has learned how to use something like seven different prosthetics in the 17 years since his accident. By taking part in this trial, he’s had to fit hundreds of hours of lab-based training and physical therapy around his demanding job. He had surgery to implant electrodes in his arm and will eventually need another to remove them. items.title: Show your library’s impact! Use the new IFLA Storytelling Manual to put your work on the map
items.raw_text: Has your library helped address a challenge in your community? Have its activities made a difference in people’s lives? If so, that is a story worth telling, you just need to bring it to life. IFLA presents the fully revised edition of Libraries and the Sustainable Development Goals: A Storytelling Manual , a practical resource to help librarians and library advocates develop, write and share compelling stories about their projects and their contributions to sustainable development. Every library has a story worth telling – events, workshops, community meetings, language clubs, collaborations are all ways libraries contribute to improving lives of the communities they serve. And by helping people access information, gain knowledge, develop skills and connect with opportunities, libraries advance sustainable development every day. Yet these contributions are not always visible or recognised by decision-makers and other stakeholders. Stories backed up by evidence can help change that, showing the difference libraries make in a clear manner to those who can support and strengthen their work. From library activities to demonstrating impact The new manual builds on the first edition of IFLA’s SDG Storytelling Manual, which supported libraries around the world in telling the stories of their projects hand the changes they helped bring about in their communities. items.title: IFLA Volunteer Model Review: Sharing Survey Results
items.raw_text: The result from three surveys run in the context of IFLA’s volunteer model review, itself part of IFLA’s Sustainable Futures Journey, shed helpful light on the experience of volunteers, their employers and our members. They underline strong points, but also areas for improvement. IFLA’s Sustainable Futures Journey is a set of steps that IFLA’s Governing Board has launched with the goal of ensuring that our Federation is in the best possible shape to continue to deliver on its strategy and missions into its second century. A major part of this is the review of our volunteering model, which is the driver of so much of what we do. In order to meet the expectations of volutneers current and future, their employers, our members, our partners, and the wider library field, we need to make sure that we have a model that delivers. As a first step in this process, we have run a series of surveys, alongside focus groups and informal conversations, targeting different groups of identified stakeholders. We are very grateful to all those who took the time to respond, and are happy now to share the results. First survey: all stakeholders Our initial survey received 475 responses, and helped to underline the strong value that people place on the uniquely international nature of engaging with IFLA, with this providing possibilities to learn and network. items.title: Now Available For 22 European Nations: Public Libraries and Information: 2025 Factsheets
items.raw_text: From PL2030: The new edition of the PL2030 Factsheets, built on 2025 data, is out. Each country’s factsheet has two parts: the first presents key data on public libraries, while the second draws on the European Parliament’s Flash Eurobarometer Social Media Survey 2025 to show where people in Europe get their information on social and political affairs, and how often they feel exposed to disinformation. Together, they place library figures next to the media habits that make information literacy matter. Direct to PL2030 Factsheets The post Now Available For 22 European Nations: Public Libraries and Information: 2025 Factsheets appeared first on Library Journal infoDOCKET .

items.title: Bibliotheek Midden-Brabant bereikt 55-plussers met papieren Digikrant
items.raw_text: Hoe bereik je inwoners die niet vanzelfsprekend online naar informatie zoeken? Bibliotheek Midden-Brabant koos bewust voor een analoog middel en ontwikkelde een eigen papieren Digikrant. De krant viel op zaterdag 21 november huis-aan-huis op de deurmat bij veel 55-plussers in de regio. De uitgave is ontwikkeld in het kader van de Week van Digitaal Meedoen en richt zich specifiek op inwoners die minder actief zijn op digitale kanalen. Met het acht pagina’s tellende blad wil de bibliotheek de drempel verlagen en laten zien welke digitale ondersteuning er in de buurt beschikbaar is. Verhalen en herkenbare ervaringen In de Digikrant staan persoonlijke verhalen van cursisten, bezoekers, medewerkers en digivrijwilligers centraal. Zo vertellen deelnemers uit onder meer Loon op Zand, Goirle, Waalwijk en Hilvarenbeek hoe cursussen en inloopspreekuren hen helpen om zelfstandiger te worden — van het herkennen van WhatsApp-fraude en het installeren van de 9292-app tot het zelf regelen van zaken via DigiD. Ook delen vrijwilligers en informatiemedewerkers hoe zij bezoekers stap voor stap en zonder haast op weg helpen. Naast de ervaringsverhalen biedt de krant een overzicht van het volledige aanbod rondom digitale vaardigheden in de zes gemeenten van het werkgebied. items.raw_text: Among the many already existing effects of AI has been a great de-individualization. I open a YouTube video, and I hear Claude. I sit in a conference presentation, and I hear Claude. I open my email inbox, and I find pitches and articles from ostensibly serious people with ostensibly serious credentials attached to ostensibly serious institutions who want to publish things attached to their reputations and mine, and I see Claude . — Jack Despain Zhou , Spitting in the Face of Glaude Tags: ai-misuse , claude , generative-ai , ai , llms

items.raw_text: Maria Hetty van den Berg is taalkundig onderwijsspecialist, conceptontwikkelaar en fictie-auteur, actief in de preventie van laaggeletterdheid. Zij schreef het handboek Liefde voor letters en lezen en de prentenboeken Alfje , het letterbeest en Alfje en het vreesmonster . Columnisten / bloggers schrijven op persoonlijke titel en weerspiegelen niet noodzakelijkerwijs het standpunt van de redactie. Als klein meisje wist ik op de basisschool niet hoe ik moest leren. Er was thuis weinig aandacht voor en ik kreeg aan het einde van de rit de huishoudschool geadviseerd. Wat mij heeft gered? De jeugdbibliotheek, die ik van voor tot achter heb uitgelezen. Dankzij die boeken bouwde ik een enorme woordenschat op. Toen ik eenmaal ontdekte hóe je moest leren, ging de rest bijna vanzelf. Ik weet dus uit eigen ervaring hoe cruciaal veel lezen is. Maar ik weet inmiddels ook hoeveel gevaar je loopt om laaggeletterd de basisschool te verlaten als de brede basis van geletterdheid in de vroege jaren ontbreekt. Vandaag de dag loopt nog altijd één op de tien kinderen het risico laaggeletterd de maatschappij in te gaan. Dat is onacceptabel. items.title: Wat kunnen Nederlandse bibliotheken leren van Denemarken als het gaat om democratie en burgerschap?
items.raw_text: Wat maakt Denemarken voor bibliotheken een inspirerend voorbeeld voor democratie en burgerschap? Met een projectsubsidie van Erasmus+ kon Probiblio dit in een paar dagen verkennen bij maatschappelijke organisaties in Aarhus, Kopenhagen en Roskilde. In dit verslag lees je de eerste bevindingen. Tekst: Thomas de Bruin, adviseur marketing en communicatie bij Probiblio De 4 belangrijkste inzichten die we hebben opgedaan •Gebruik hyperlokale thema’s in je programma’s. Dit verlaagt de drempel en vergroot de motivatie om deel te nemen. Zoek, waar dat kan, de verbinding tussen hyperlokale thema’s en wereldwijde vraagstukken. Een voorbeeld van zo’n thema was een overstroomd fietspad en het gesprek met alle omwonenden over klimaatverandering en de impact op hun leefomgeving. •Om ervoor te zorgen dat je programmering toegankelijk is, ook voor mensen die zich minder makkelijk uitdrukken in gesproken taal, kun je beweging gebruiken als middel. Laat deelnemers opstaan en zitten, zich verplaatsen door de ruimte, stickers plakken en in kleine groepjes werken, zodat iedereen gehoord wordt. •Communiceer altijd helder wat mensen komen doen, wat het doel en mandaat is van de organisator. Dit zorgt voor duidelijkheid bij iedereen en voorkomt situaties die lastig te modereren zijn voor begeleiders. •Besteed zichtbaar aandacht aan democratie en burgerschap, zodat mensen ervaren dat democratie iets is om trots op te zijn en actief aan deel te nemen. items.title: Behind the Counter: What a National Survey Reveals About Public Library Staff in Spain
items.raw_text: A new report published by Spain’s Ministry of Culture looks closely at the people who keep the country’s libraries running. La realidad profesional del personal de las bibliotecas de titularidad pública en España (“The professional reality of staff in publicly owned libraries in Spain”) was prepared by the Professional Development Working Group of the Spanish Library Cooperation Council (Consejo de Cooperación Bibliotecaria). The study was led by Carlos Miguel Tejada Artigas (Universidad Complutense de Madrid). It is based on a nationwide survey answered by 2,604 professionals working in all types of publicly owned libraries. Public libraries make up the largest group: 45.4% of respondents work in municipal libraries and a further 4.4% in regional public libraries. Because results are broken down by library type, the study shows clearly where public libraries resemble the rest of the system and where they stand apart. Highly qualified staff working below their qualifications Across the whole sample, 90.2% hold a university degree, far above the average for Spain’s working population. Only 27.8% hold a degree in Library and Information Science, and 91% say they have needed continuing education during their careers. Qualifications and job grades do not match: only 60.7% of civil-servant librarians hold posts that formally require a university degree. The gap is most visible in municipal libraries. items.title: Blog: Xylotheek?
items.raw_text: Janneke Krommendijk werkte ruim 46 jaar in de bibliotheekwereld. 25 jaar als assistent-bibliothecaresse bij de bibliotheek Almelo en daarna 22 jaar als mediathecaris op CCG Reggesteyn in Nijverdal. Ze vindt het eeuwig zonde als kennis verloren gaat… Columnisten / bloggers schrijven op persoonlijke titel en weerspiegelen niet noodzakelijkerwijs het standpunt van de redactie. Heeft u er wel eens van gehoord? Tot op vandaag ik in elk geval niet. We kennen er veel: noem Bibliotheek, Mediatheek, Speel-o-theek, Apotheek, Artotheek, Discotheek, er zijn er nog wel meer vermoed ik. Het gaat om gangbare begrippen voor instellingen of organisaties in onze samenleving. Meestal weet je ook direct waar je mee te maken hebt. Biblios komt uit het Grieks en betekent ‘boek’ en verwijst “Arto’ naar kunst. Het gaat om collecties, verzamelingen die je kunt bekijken en of waaruit je mogelijks iets kunt lenen, al dan niet tegen betaling. Maar een Xylotheek ? Dat is een ander verhaal. Xulon komt uit het Grieks en betekent hout. Een houtbibliotheek dus. Hoe zien we dat voor ons? Een verzameling boeken, wat eigenlijk houten doosjes zijn, met het uiterlijk van een boek. Aan de rug- en voorzijde beplakt met boomschors van de boomsoort waar het ‘boek’ over gaat. In het doosje een beschrijving van de boom, gedroogde blaadjes, vruchten, etc. Alles over die desbetreffende boomsoort uitvoerig gedocumenteerd bij elkaar. items.title: Towards the futures we want: IFLA comes to Mexico City
items.raw_text: IFLA will reach a key milestone in our progress towards our centennial Congress with a set of events in Mexico City in April 2027. What can we be doing today to maximise the chances of achieving the future we want for libraries and knowledge, and what even is this future? And what does this mean for how we approach key international frameworks such as the post-2030 Agenda? These will be the key questions in focus when IFLA’s Governing Board comes to Mexico City on 26-29 April 2027. The National Autonomous University of Mexico (UNAM) has kindly agreed to host a series of events in addition to the Board meetings, making it possible to engage with the Mexican and wider Latin American and Caribbean library communities, check in on all of the discussions taking place as part of IFLA100, and look ahead both to IFLA’s 2027 Congress and the SDG Summit that will kick-start the preparation of what comes after the UN’s 2030 Agenda and its Sustainable Development Goals. In addition to meetings of the Board itself, we are planning on events for the wider field, drawing on expertise from inside and outside the field, designed around engagement and conversation with colleagues. UNAM itself is one of the world’s largest universities, and hosts the Institute for Library and Information Research (IIBI), a key centre for reflection on libraries and information, their place in society, and relation to emerging issues. items.title: IFLA Regional Offices 2027-2029: Hosts announced
items.raw_text: At its most recent formal meeting, IFLA’s Governing Board took its decision about the hosts of IFLA’s Regional Offices for Asia-Oceania, Latin America and the Caribbean, the Middle East and North Africa, and Sub-Saharan Africa for 2027-2029. IFLA’s Regional Offices are hosted by institutions committed to enabling the full participation of libraries and library and information workers in their region in the work of IFLA. They have an important role both in helping colleagues around the world benefit from belonging to an international field, as well as ensuring that our Headquarters and wider organisation are aware of key issues and needs. They have been a part of IFLA’s operation for many years already, and indeed as part of our work to put more of IFLA’s archives online , you can now dig into some of the back catalogues of newsletters and other work they have done. Today, in the context of our Sustainable Futures Journey , they not only fulfil their traditional role, but have a mission to be hubs, not only for learning and sharing between professionals, but also for libraries to meet and form links with external partners, including funders. They serve a three-year term, with the current one coming to an end at the end of this year, and work with IFLA Headquarters, as well as coordinating with the relevant Regional Division Committee. items.raw_text: Volvo provided flights from Washington, DC, to Copenhagen, Denmark, and accommodation so Ars could drive the XC60 and XC90 plug-in hybrids. Ars does not accept paid editorial content. COPENHAGEN, Denmark—If we lived in the world that Volvo’s product planners expected back when the current XC90 debuted in 2015 , both it and the smaller but related XC60 (which arrived in 2017) might have been the last of their kind as everything went electric . As we know, the future hasn’t turned out quite like that, especially in the critically important US market . At the same time, Europe and China are electrifying, which seems like an argument against spending resources on developing all-new replacements for models that might not have an eight-year lifespan in most markets. So instead, Volvo has given the XC60 and XC90 another lifecycle refresh. The exterior styling tweaks are minimal; the bigger three-row XC90 had already been given a new look last year, and the XC60 now gains a similar grille and the same matrix headlights, for instance. And that’s no bad thing—both were, and remain, handsome shapes that are popular with Volvo’s customer base. Instead, the Swedish automaker’s attention has been on bringing the technology up to date for model year 2028 standards. Which means a much bigger battery for the PHEVs, with sufficient capacity for a couple of days of daily driving for most of us before needing to be recharged. items.title: Ford unveils the GT41 as it hopes to win Le Mans again
items.raw_text: Sixty years ago, after two failed attempts, Ford won the 24 Hours of Le Mans with its GT40 race car. In the years since, the Blue Oval has been back to France more than a few times, with varying success. It could never replicate the GT40’s success winning overall, but it celebrated the 40th anniversary with a class win . Now it wants another shot at the really big trophy , and it debuted the car during the Detroit Lions-Chicago Bears football game today: meet the GT41. “Revealing the Ford GT41 is a significant moment for everyone involved in this program,” said Dan Sayers, manager of Ford Racing’s Hypercar program. “It's the result of an enormous amount of work across our engineering, design, and development teams and an important milestone on our journey towards 2027. We know the scale of the challenge ahead—the level of competition in Hypercar is incredibly high, and there are no shortcuts to success. Our focus has been on building the right foundations, bringing together the right people and making sure we learn as much as possible from every stage of development.” The video was directed by Zack Snyder and features Matt Damon’s voice-over. Met die vraag stapten negen vrijwilligers en twee medewerkers van Bibliotheek Twello op een koude winterochtend op de fiets richting Rijnbrink in Deventer. Toen de kaart van het werkgebied werd getoond, volgden meteen de eerste vragen. ‘Bedienen jullie dit hele gebied?’ Veel deelnemers realiseerden zich op dat moment pas hoe groot het gebied is waarin dagelijks boeken reizen. items.title: Politieacademie werkt aan slimme databank voor cold cases
items.raw_text: Onderzoekers van de Politieacademie, Hogeschool Saxion en de Universiteit Twente werken aan een nieuwe databank die rechercheurs moet helpen bij het reconstrueren van misdrijven en het oplossen van oude moordzaken (cold cases). De databank moet gegevens uit politiedossiers, 3D-reconstructies van plaatsen delict, sensordata en open source intelligence combineren. Op termijn moeten met ai op basis van die gegevens automatisch de meest waarschijnlijke scenario’s van een misdrijf naar boven komen. Dat vertelde Jaap Knotter, lector aan de Politieacademie en Saxion Applied University. Hij is hoofd van het joint lectoraat Technologies for Criminal Investigations (TCI). Computable sprak hem tijdens een bijeenkomst in Deventer waar een nieuwe methode voor het digitaal vastleggen van plaatsen delict werd gedemonstreerd. Knotter legt uit dat rechercheurs in ieder onderzoek antwoord moeten zien te vinden op de zogenoemde zeven gouden W-vragen: wie, wat, waar, waarmee, op welke wijze, wanneer en waarom. Die vragen vormen de basis voor het verhaal dat uiteindelijk door een officier van justitie wordt gepresenteerd en waarop een rechter zijn oordeel baseert. ‘Het verhaal is cruciaal’, benadrukt Knotter. ‘Op de genoemde vragen wil je antwoord hebben.
